content:
Meta continues to take its artificial intelligence technology seriously. The latest sign? A dedicated Meta AI Mac app.

Meta enters the competitive Mac AI app market

The brand-new Meta AI desktop app launches as a 1.0 beta and takes up only 16MB after installation.

Based on initial observations, the app runs natively on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later, using the AppKit and SwiftUI frameworks alongside WebKit to deliver richer conversational content. In other words, this is not an Electron app, nor a repackaged iPad version.

It includes Mac-specific feature integrations, making the desktop experience more complete than the Meta AI mobile app.

Quick Invoke uses the Option-Space keys to open a streamlined Meta AI writing window on any workspace. Another dictation feature lets you hold a shortcut to speak and have your voice converted into text input for any app—from emails and documents to code editors.

Meta AI can also attach another Mac window to the conversation. With screen recording and accessibility permissions, the app can read the text visible in the window and capture screenshots to serve as reference material for the next question. For now, this is a context-gathering feature, not a computer control one.

Beyond the conversation feature, the sidebar also includes media, Artifacts, scheduled tasks, conversation history, and an "About Me" personalisation section.

Users can switch between different thinking modes, attach files, generate media content, and create recurring briefings or reminders. The app also offers the option to hide the Dock icon, allowing users to launch it via keyboard shortcuts.

Meta's recent AI developments

The Mac app is the latest in a string of ongoing new releases. In April, Meta replaced Llama with Muse Spark. The May update brought more natural voice conversations and camera-based real-time assistance to Meta AI.

In July, Meta brought Muse-powered image generation to Meta AI, WhatsApp, and Instagram—though Meta subsequently removed one feature that generated images using public Instagram posts. Meta AI also arrived on Threads direct messages, offering private chat services.

More recently, Meta launched Muse Code, a terminal-based AI coding agent for macOS and Linux.
